final_answer: When an mRNA vaccine is injected into the muscle, the mRNA enters nearby cells. These cells use the mRNA as a blueprint to produce a harmless piece of the virus, such as the spike protein. The spike protein is then displayed on the cell's surface, which signals the immune system to recognize it as foreign. The immune system responds by producing antibodies and activating T-cells to fight off the perceived threat. Importantly, the mRNA is temporary and is broken down by the body after it has done its job. This process trains the immune system to recognize and attack the actual virus if encountered in the future, providing protection without causing disease. Safe.
